location_system.corridor_definition: A corridor is a linear path or area between two known points. Context determines whether it is safe, dangerous, or otherwise. Ruled 2026-09-19, Ruling 2. The corridor classes are NOT a safety gradient - they sort by who built or uses a corridor and what it leads to.
location_system.shard_progression_note: Flicker -> Ghostwave -> Fracture -> Rupture is the shard progression: a severity scale layering over places. It is NOT a spatial taxonomy and contributes nothing to ENV. Ruling 1.

milestone_grid._act_note: A1-A3 are the three acts. Every book has exactly three, and 27 acts remains the cap. PR and EP are STRUCTURAL POSITIONS OUTSIDE the act model, not additional acts - a prologue or epilogue occupies this slot without being counted as an act. Ruled 2026-09-20, GATE_RULINGS_2026-09-20.md Ruling 6. This supersedes the previous note, which called EP an invalid act and reported the five EP rows as notices; under Ruling 6 that framing was wrong.
milestone_grid._thread_note: RECONCILED 2026-09-20 (Ruling 7) from two lists that were on file: ledger 43 section 2 proposed veil/mt/tahl/silence_hope/institutions/filaments/caro_elisabet; the 09-20 open-items proposal section 2 proposed the POV baton leads plus the faction lines. The union is taken, with three changes. (1) `veil` becomes `world` - `veil` collides with T1's name, and the thread is the world's condition, not the trilogy. (2) `institutions` splits into `dominion`, `technarc` and `choirless`: grouping them cannot distinguish B08's Technarc collapse from its neighbours, and resolution is the whole point of the column. (3) The POV leads `seraphine`, `baz` and `kade` are added; ledger 43's list omitted them. `mt` is KEPT as distinct from `tahl`: the channel's own arc - anonymous, named, passed to Kade, renamed LT - outlives the person carrying it. PROVISIONAL.
milestone_grid._pressure_note: RENAMED 2026-09-20 from pressure_before/pressure_after. Ruled: "World pressure should not effect romance." Each row's pressure measures ITS OWN thread, so a romance milestone is scored on the romance thread and a world milestone on the world thread. This is what ledger 43 section 2 found the column already doing inconsistently: five rows open BELOW the previous row's close (M04, M07, M09, M17, M18), which is impossible for a single world scale and ordinary once each row is read against its own thread. WARNING, and it is the reason every row is still `proposed`: the 36 existing values were scored BEFORE this column existed, so their provenance is MIXED - some are world readings, some thread readings. The rename states the intended meaning; it does not certify the values. Rows carrying a non-`world` thread need re-scoring.

pressure_scale._ruling: Ruled 2026-09-20: "the intent is to be flexible and allow escalation within a trilogy not be defined by an overly restrictive system. If needed increase the number of levels or redefine by each trilogy, etc."
pressure_scale.calibration: PER TRILOGY (Ruling 7 of 2026-09-20). A 5 in Veil does not denote the same magnitude as a 5 in Loom. The scale is NOT saga-absolute and must not be compared across trilogies without calibration.
pressure_scale._extensible_note: The ceiling is not fixed at 5. T2 currently uses only 4 and 5 across three books, which is compression, not escalation; widening the scale or rebasing T2 is permitted and needs no further ruling. T1 already spans 1-5 and T3 spans 1-5 (distinct 1,3,4,5), so T2 is the only compressed trilogy.
pressure_scale._direction_note: Trilogies do not all run the same way. T1 and T2 RISE; T3 FALLS - it opens at its maximum in B07 and ends at its minimum after the Mending. Any per-trilogy anchoring must define 1 as the trilogy's MINIMUM and 5 as its MAXIMUM, never as "opening" and "peak": for T3 the opening IS the peak, and the opening-baseline form would invert the scale.

grid_purposes._status: Recorded 2026-09-20 so two grids cannot end up scoring the same quantity twice. Ledger section 64.
grid_purposes.grids/milestones_payoffs.csv: NARRATIVE pressure, per thread. `thread_pressure_before/after` measure the thread named in that row's `thread` column - what is happening in the story. Calibrated per trilogy, extensible (see milestone_grid.pressure_scale).
grid_purposes.grids/reader_pressure.csv: READER-FACING intensity, per cohort. Its own columns say so: reader_group, pressure_state, intensity_1_5, over an episode_range. This is how hard the READER is being squeezed, which is a different quantity from how bad things are in the story, and the two diverge - a quiet scene can be the most intense to read. Header-only; canon/editorial_lenses.md and rules/validation_checks.json both already point at it.
grid_purposes._why_both: The 2026-09-19 derivation draft framed these as alternatives - make pressure per-thread OR split the axis into a reader grid. They are not alternatives. Threading fixes WHOSE pressure a milestone records; the reader grid answers a question the milestone grid never asks. Ruled 2026-09-20: keep both, and score a quantity in exactly one of them.

retired_terms._note: Names retired by ruling. tools/validate_canon.py CHK_RETIRED_TERMS reports any match as a VIOLATION in canon scope and a NOTICE in all-scope (recovery/, proposals/, reports/, decisions/, CLAUDE.md), where quoting a retired name as evidence is legitimate. Matching is case-insensitive and whole-word, so capitalised headings are caught. Added 2026-09-25, ledger 76. Mortal Technology is deliberately ABSENT: the MT reconciliation is open, so that name is held, not retired.
